beats.lead: Nintendo feels like a modern company
beats.text: It was founded in 1889, making playing cards.
beats.note: Hand-painted hanafuda (Japanese flower cards) crafted from mulberry bark in a Kyoto workshop. It is still headquartered in Kyoto today.

beats.name: Fusajiro Yamauchi
beats.role: He opened the shop as Nintendo Koppai. By 1929 it was the largest card maker in Japan, and in 1959 a deal with Disney put Mickey Mouse on the decks: a record 600,000 sold that year.

beats.context: From that first deck of flower cards to the Game Boy of 1989, a full century before Nintendo's most famous handheld.

beats.lead: In between, it tried almost anything
beats.text: In the 1960s it ran a taxi firm and sold instant rice.
beats.note: Flush from going public, Nintendo sold packets of instant rice (a flop), ran the Daiya taxi company, and even opened an hourly-rental hotel, before deciding toys and games were its future.

beats.text: For its first eighty years, the maker of Mario never sold a single video game.

beats.line: It dealt flower cards for a century before pixels.
